title: fix: leftover SQLite snapshot copies from Doctor and triage are never reclaimed
body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193174, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193652

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: SQLite snapshot copies that Doctor or `openclaw triage` fail to remove are never reclaimed. On top of that, every run leaves a new empty `~/Library/Caches/openclaw/sqlite-<hash>/` directory.

On one Mac host, 49 GB of leftover copies from two triage runs sat in `sqlite-0e5d8581…` and `sqlite-ac549b06…`. The installation's own namespace (`sqlite-9565507d…`, the one its Gateway sweeps) was empty.

## User Impact

Snapshot copies taken during Doctor and triage now live in the installation's own namespace. If one is left behind by a crash, a kill or a failed cleanup, the Gateway's existing snapshot reclamation removes it after its usual grace period. Runs no longer add an empty namespace directory each time.

This PR does not remove copies that are already on disk in older per-run namespaces. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193652 does that: the Gateway sweep also reclaims day-old copies in sibling namespaces and directly under the cache parent.

## Why This Change Was Made

Doctor lint inspects a private copy of the state directory. That copy is a snapshot staged inside the installation's namespace, and Doctor points `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` at it. The snapshot namespace is a hash of the resolved state directory, so every snapshot taken in that context went into a namespace hashed from the throwaway path. That's a new one per run, and the Gateway's sweep (`reclaimAbandonedSqliteSnapshots`) only looks in the installation's namespace.

`resolveSnapshotStagingRoot` now reuses the enclosing namespace when the resolved state directory is strictly inside an existing `sqlite-<24 hex>` namespace under the admitted cache root. Any other state directory, including a different installation sharing the cache, keeps its own hashed namespace. Reclamation still takes each snapshot's lifetime token before deleting it, so copies that are in use stay fenced.

This is independent of PR #193174, which fixes the cleanup failure when an inspection task is cancelled. This PR makes sure anything that still escapes cleanup can be reclaimed.

## Evidence

Head `064f66db2bc2`, which contains `origin/main` `2c04aec4eb6f`. The latest main merge doesn't touch the SQLite staging, temp-root or state-dir paths.

Reproduction in a disposable HOME and state dir, logging every `sqlite-<hash>` namespace created and the `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` at that moment:
- Base: each triage or Doctor run created a fresh namespace (`ca81928c…`, `5c9aaece…`, `afc816a0…`, `b976225e…` across runs). Its `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` was `…/sqlite-<install>/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-*/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-*/openclaw-state`.
- This branch: two `triage --run` runs left only the installation's namespace.

Regression test in `src/infra/sqlite-private-directory.test.ts`: "keeps a private state copy in its enclosing namespace but hashes any other cache path". A private state copy at `<namespace>/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-*/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-*/openclaw-state` resolves to that namespace.

Negative controls in the same case: a state dir equal to the namespace itself, and one at `<cache>/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-*/openclaw-state` (outside any namespace), each get their own hashed `sqlite-<24 hex>` namespace. The cache root holds exactly those three namespaces. The unchanged case "isolates installations sharing a cache and keeps each namespace stable" still covers separate installations.
- base: fails (the private state copy gets a new hashed namespace)
- accepting the namespace itself (`inside.length >= 0`): fails (`expected 2 to be 3`)
- accepting any enclosing directory, not just `sqlite-<24 hex>`: fails (the outside path resolves to `openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-aB3dE6`)
- this branch: passes

Commands:
- `pnpm test` on the 31 files touching the staging root, reclamation, retirement, read-only location cleanup, update-candidate state and Doctor lint state: 220 passed (first revision).
- After adding the controls and merging main: `vitest run` on every test file that calls `resolvePrivateSqliteSnapshotStagingRoot` or Doctor's lint state snapshot. One case failed under load: "preserves cold DB and sidecar names and bytes through full authority (profile=true)" in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-github-readiness.test.ts`. It passed when rerun alone, both on this branch and with this PR's source reverted. After the last main merge, which changed `tmp-openclaw-dir.ts`, `sqlite-private-directory`, `tmp-openclaw-dir` and `doctor-session-archive-cache-check` tests: 42 passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: lint, format and import-cycle guards pass. Madge: 0 cycles. The local tsgo typecheck can't run on this machine because the checkout uses the shared pnpm store, which its graph boundary refuses. CI's typecheck is the gate for that: on `007d709c2f58` it caught an unchecked tuple index in the new test (`check-test-types-core-3`), fixed in `064f66db2bc2` by typing the names `as const`.
- Test-lines ratchet: net growth +25, recorded exactly in `config/test-lines-allocations/sqlite-snapshot-private-state-namespace.txt`. The check passes (slack 11).
- Autoreview (Codex, branch mode against `origin/main`, P0–P2): scoped-clean on `96d0ecc8bfa3` (before the last main merge).

Test file audit (`src/infra/sqlite-private-directory.test.ts`, read in full): the new case reuses the existing temp-dir tracker and owns its cache root. The earlier revision's assertions moved out of "isolates installations…", which is back to its original form. Nothing was pruned.
